body.en: India became an exporter of primary products such as raw silk, cotton, wool, sugar, indigo and jute, and an importer of finished consumer goods like cotton, silk and woollen clothes and of capital goods like light machinery from British factories. Britain kept a monopoly: more than half of India's *trade* was with Britain. The opening of the Suez Canal in 1869 made this trade cheaper and faster.
body.kn: ಭಾರತ ಕಚ್ಚಾ ರೇಷ್ಮೆ, ಹತ್ತಿ, ಉಣ್ಣೆ, ಸಕ್ಕರೆ, ನೀಲಿ, ಸೆಣಬು ಮುಂತಾದ ಪ್ರಾಥಮಿಕ ವಸ್ತುಗಳನ್ನು ರಫ್ತು ಮಾಡಿ ಬ್ರಿಟನ್‌ನ ಸಿದ್ಧ ವಸ್ತುಗಳನ್ನು ಆಮದು ಮಾಡುತ್ತಿತ್ತು. ಅರ್ಧಕ್ಕಿಂತ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ವ್ಯಾಪಾರ ಬ್ರಿಟನ್ ಜೊತೆಗಿತ್ತು.

title.en: Export surplus and drain of wealth

body.en: India had a large *export surplus*, but it did not bring gold or silver into the country. It was used to pay for the colonial government's office expenses in Britain, its war expenses and the import of invisible items. This outflow is called the drain of Indian wealth, and it caused shortages of food grains, kerosene and other essentials at home.
body.kn: ಭಾರತಕ್ಕೆ ರಫ್ತು ಹೆಚ್ಚುವರಿ ಇದ್ದರೂ ಅದು ಬ್ರಿಟಿಷ್ ಆಡಳಿತದ ಕಚೇರಿ ವೆಚ್ಚ, ಯುದ್ಧ ವೆಚ್ಚ ಮತ್ತು ಅದೃಶ್ಯ ಆಮದುಗಳಿಗೆ ಖರ್ಚಾಯಿತು. ಇದೇ ಭಾರತದ ಸಂಪತ್ತಿನ ಸೋರಿಕೆ.

problem.en: In a year a colony exports goods worth ₹500 crore and imports goods worth ₹380 crore. Of the surplus, ₹90 crore pays colonial office and war expenses abroad and ₹30 crore pays for invisible imports. How much of the surplus stays in the colony?

answer.en: Nothing stays: the whole ₹120 crore surplus drains out, exactly the colonial pattern.

narration.en: Let us work through this together. In a year a colony exports goods worth ₹500 crore and imports goods worth ₹380 crore. Of the surplus, ₹90 crore pays colonial office and war expenses abroad and ₹30 crore pays for invisible imports. How much of the surplus stays in the colony?

say.en: Let us work through this together. In a year a colony exports goods worth 500 rupees crore and imports goods worth 380 rupees crore. Of the surplus, 90 rupees crore pays colonial office and war expenses abroad and 30 rupees crore pays for invisible imports. How much of the surplus stays in the colony?
Export surplus equals 500 minus 380 equals 120 rupees crore.
Outflow equals 90 plus 30 equals 120 rupees crore.
Retained equals 120 minus 120 equals 0 rupees.
So the answer is Nothing stays: the whole 120 rupees crore surplus drains out, exactly the colonial pattern.

say.en: Competitive exam practice: CUET-pattern questions. Read every option before you choose. A colony exports goods worth 640 rupees crore and imports 450 rupees crore. It pays 150 rupees crore abroad for office, war and invisible expenses. How much of the export surplus is retained at home?
Export surplus equals 640 minus 450 equals 190 rupees crore.
Retained equals 190 minus 150 equals 40 rupees crore; the 150 rupees crore paid abroad is the drain.
